paper_title: Development and validation of self-monitoring auto-updating prognostic models of survival for hospitalized COVID-19 patients
prediction_task: 7-day and 28-day survival prediction for COVID-19 with dynamic model updating

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: How to use multiple imputation in a prospective setting for both individual risk prediction and model updating? How to predict mortality for a patient who misses some predictor values? How to include patients with missing predictors in model updating?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added detailed description of real-time imputation strategy using last-observation-carried-forward and mean imputation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: XGBoost coefficients in Figure 5 — how were they derived and why are they all positive? Also, lactate and log-transformed lactate both included is hard to interpret — were original and log-transformed predictors in variable selection simultaneously?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified XGBoost feature importance (not coefficients). Removed log-transformed duplicate.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Line 184, please explain how the 'minority class was oversampled to correct for class imbalance'. Multiple technical terms unexplained: one-hot encoded, passive imputation, AUPR, ICI.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added explanations of all technical terms and detailed oversampling methodology.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Slightly uncertain how much small model performance drifts impact on clinical care when models are used as adjunct only. Practicalities and cost of applying and maintaining the dynamic updating system on larger scale not well discussed.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added discussion of implementation cost and clinical impact of calibration drift.

reviewer_strengths.text: Interesting work with a large dataset. Well designed study incorporating comparable validation models. Potential benefits over static models clearly described.
